Priya (CS): Hey @Carlos — quick Q from the onboarding questionnaire: your security team marked PCI data in scope for the integration. Can you confirm which endpoints will touch PANs or card tokens?
Nina (Security): @Priya /cc @Ethan we need to know if card data is stored, masked, or proxied to a payment gateway. If you only pass a token to Redwood and we never persist raw PAN, that narrows scope a lot.
Carlos (Customer): We proxy to Stripe. We only send a Stripe token to your API, we do not give you raw card numbers. Is that enough for you to mark PCI out of scope?
Ethan (Solutions): Good sign. In our onboarding matrix we ask two things: 1) raw PAN present? 2) any ability to decrypt or reconstruct tokens? If both no, we can annotate as "payment-token-only" and exclude PCI processing in the vendor form.
Priya (CS): @Carlos please confirm: are tokens occasionally logged in traces or passed to support tickets? Small logging can reintroduce scope.
Carlos (Customer): We redacted tokens in logs but have a short-lived debug flag that dumps request bodies in staging. Production logs are redacted.
Nina (Security): That debug flag is the red flag. We need assurance it's off for prod and not accessible to CS/Support. Two asks: (a) turn off debug in prod or ensure it redacts tokens, (b) provide a short statement from infra saying debug flag is disabled for prod.
Priya (CS): I'll draft the questionnaire reply once we have the infra note. Suggest a 1-2 line statement like: "We do not store or log raw PANs; only payment-provider tokens are sent to Redwood. Debug flag is disabled in prod."
Ethan (Solutions): Also add a line about retention: tokens are ephemeral, TTL <30d, and are not used for reconciliation. That helps the auditor.
Carlos (Customer): Ok I can get infra to sign something. ETA EOD today.
OnboardBot: Reminder: attach the signed infra statement to the "security-evidence" ticket #ONB-512 before closing the questionnaire. :bell:
Priya (CS): Awesome — once we have the statement I'll push the completed vendor form back to legal and mark renewal risk low. Thanks all :tada:
